candidates.opened_evidence: NumPy documents an ndarray return, copy=False rejecting necessary copies, and the __dlpack__/__dlpack_device__ protocol. Its CPU import example demonstrates producer mutation visible in the NumPy view; a reverse example exports a NumPy array to PyTorch.
candidates.remaining_adapter: Connect supported producer objects at the numerical-library boundary and respect ownership, device and mutability constraints. The complete standardized namespace remains separate.
candidates.limitations: Examples were read, not executed. Default copy=None may copy; strict no-copy use requires copy=False and exporter support. The guide describes read-only imported arrays and restrictions on exporting read-only inputs. Unsupported dtypes/layouts and all lifetime edge cases were not tested.

selection_rationale: Prepared exactly two candidates and three distinct cited documents. NumPy's concrete no-copy ndarray exchange is the closest exact independent action; array-api-strict offers broader namespace behavior with declared target/version gaps. Supplier consumer docs and interoperability examples outrank mirrors; an actually delivered common link supplied the strict implementation. No fourth body request was needed.
